section_summary.extract_value: The Results describe factorial validity testing of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) in a single sample (N = 2393), comparing one-dimensional and multiple two-factor models and arriving at a best-fitting two-factor solution after removing four items. The structure was invariant across sex, General Body Appreciation showed good internal consistency, women showed a moderate negative correlation with BMI (r = -0.32) while men showed no significant BMI correlation (r = -0.02).

section_summary.extract_value: This Results section reports confirmatory factor analyses of the BAS (N = 2393), showing that a two-factor model with four items removed (#1, 7, 11, 12) provided the best fit and that the factor structure was invariant across sex. Internal consistency was strong for the General Body Appreciation factor (α_women = .92, α_men = .90) but poor for the Body Image Investment factor, which was omitted; women showed a negative correlation between General Body Appreciation and BMI (r = −.32) while men showed a nonsignificant correlation (r = −.02).

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports CFA model comparisons on data from a single sample (N = 2393), showing poor fit for the original one-dimensional BAS and improved fit for a two-factor model after removing four poorly performing items (#1, 7, 11, 12). The best-fitting two-factor model was invariant across sex; General Body Appreciation (the retained factor) showed high internal consistency and was higher in men than women (small effect), and was negatively correlated with BMI in women (r = -0.32) but not in men (r = -0.02). No explicit study numbering (e.g., 'Study 1') or multiple sample subsets are mentioned in this section.
